page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 32 vCPUs, corresponding to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong CPU and memory capabilities. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2187.0 and a multi-core score of 18229.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested configurations. Text processing performance is particularly high, reaching the top 10% with a Geekbench score of 2832.0. Cryptographic and compression workloads also perform strongly, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 36252.74 and single-threaded gzip compression at 34.25 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions support text generation speeds of 357.67 tokens/sec for a small 135M LLM model, placing it in the top 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the c8i.8xlarge is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for any persistent data. The 2:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio also limits its suitability for memory-bound databases. However, the high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated Intel Xeon cores provide high compute density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. This hardware profile is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
